sources: Test demand and resources; give owners measurable goals and review results.
CAC includes sales and marketing costs divided by acquired customers. Validate costs and customer value.
Historical 2021 count: 104,290 residents aged 65+. This is not a current paying market estimate.
Public assessment and private-pay care are distinct pathways. Explain existing options.
Truthful verifiable service information, clinician identity and professional boundaries; no unsupported superiority or guarantees.
Marketing uses of health information require express consent; care consent is separate.
Check the consent basis, sender identification and unsubscribe requirements before promotional email/SMS.
Public-funded service opportunities have formal qualification/procurement routes; no public contract is assumed. Search result verified; direct page retrieval returned 403.
dayConvention: Day 1 is the start date you supply. Day N = start date + N − 1 calendar days. Deadlines do not certify readiness. Review weekends, holidays, staffing and current requirements before activation.
disclaimer: Evidence informs the method and safeguards. All counts, rates, dates, prices, budgets and service thresholds below are proposed management assumptions, not published industry benchmarks or guaranteed results. No real achievements are fabricated.

tasks.title: Approve scope, roles and decision rights
tasks.description: Select one initial organization segment, decision-maker, use case and geography. Name the person covering each proposed role. Agree budget authority and pause rights.
tasks.deliverable: Signed scope and ownership map.
tasks.acceptance: No team is treated as staffed until names and availability are confirmed.

tasks.title: Interview ten potential tenant buyers
tasks.description: Arrange permission-based interviews; test unmet workflow, incumbent products, willingness to pay, procurement and switching effort.
tasks.deliverable: Ten de-identified buyer interviews and objection themes.
tasks.acceptance: Separate problems from assumed feature demand.

tasks.title: Review competitors and customer alternatives
tasks.description: Compare published provider features, manual workflows and do-nothing choices. Validate one narrow reason to change without unsupported superiority.
tasks.deliverable: Competitor/alternative comparison and testable value proposition.
tasks.acceptance: Verify claims against implemented functions and source pages.

tasks.title: Verify six core platform workflows
tasks.description: Run browser→API→database readback for identity, tenant setup, cross-tenant access denial, billing, support and recovery. Add negative/error cases and real audit correlations.
tasks.deliverable: Six test packs with defects and evidence references.
tasks.acceptance: Resolve critical isolation, onboarding or payment/readback defects before pilots.

tasks.title: Review privacy, access and commercial terms
tasks.description: Review record roles, minimum data, permission boundaries, charges, support, cancellation and incident responsibilities. Keep patient information outside this tracker.
tasks.deliverable: Reviewed data/contract versions and open issues.
tasks.acceptance: No unresolved critical legal/privacy issue before a pilot.

tasks.title: Validate price and full delivery costs
tasks.description: Use actual quotes and buyer feedback. Include hosting, voice, support, implementation, staff time, refunds and acquisition cost.
tasks.deliverable: Quote-backed cost model and proposed price.
tasks.acceptance: Illustrative CAD399/month is not a quote; validate willingness to pay.

tasks.title: Write truthful demo and accessible offer
tasks.description: Show working capabilities only. Mark demo records. Explain rollout limits, data handling, staffed support and prices before asking for a pilot.
tasks.deliverable: Demo script, service page and objection sheet.
tasks.acceptance: Product and commercial reviewers approve every claim.

tasks.title: Build 100-account research list
tasks.description: Use public organization information and lawful contact routes. Record fit, buyer role and next step; no patient lists or personal health targeting.
tasks.deliverable: 100-account segmented prospect register.
tasks.acceptance: A researched account is not a lead or consenting contact.

tasks.title: Set contact permission and suppression process
tasks.description: Check CASL bases, sender details, unsubscribe and telephone rules for chosen channels. Use requested conversations and approved institutional routes.
tasks.deliverable: Permission/suppression SOP and test records.
tasks.acceptance: No bulk outreach before route-specific review.

tasks.title: Configure pipeline and evidence definitions
tasks.description: Define discovered, contacted, qualified, demo, proposal, accepted pilot and paying active; deduplicate organizations and name owners.
tasks.deliverable: Stage definitions and weekly pipeline view.
tasks.acceptance: Written acceptance and payment evidence distinguish real outcomes.

tasks.title: Run first controlled discovery-to-demo wave
tasks.description: Approach selected suitable organizations within approved contact routes and support capacity. Review objections each week.
tasks.deliverable: Eight qualified opportunities and eight relevant demonstrations.
tasks.acceptance: Do not scale volume to conceal poor product fit.

tasks.title: Prepare the bounded pilot offer
tasks.description: Specify one usable workflow, duration, fees, success measures, data responsibilities, support and exit. Confirm institutional procurement requirements.
tasks.deliverable: Reviewed pilot proposal and acceptance template.
tasks.acceptance: A proposal is not a signed agreement or public service-provider contract.

tasks.title: Review Day 30 evidence and spending tranche
tasks.description: Compare interviews, defects, quotes and cash; release only a bounded next tranche or HOLD.
tasks.deliverable: Dated gate decision and spend cap.
tasks.acceptance: Critical defects and unaffordable commitments block expansion.

tasks.title: Obtain and implement first accepted pilots
tasks.description: Seek two written pilot acceptances. Verify product readiness, responsible contacts and safe setup before activation.
tasks.deliverable: Two genuinely accepted pilots with implementation checklists.
tasks.acceptance: No unaccepted or unready pilot is counted.

tasks.title: Train tenant managers and verify activation
tasks.description: Guide first tenant setup, role checks, a complete usable workflow, error recovery and human support route.
tasks.deliverable: Activation evidence and tenant training guide.
tasks.acceptance: Tenant manager can repeat the workflow independently.

tasks.title: Measure actual support effort and incidents
tasks.description: Record staffed response, unresolved errors, onboarding time, actual voice/tool costs and recovery. Review each pilot weekly.
tasks.deliverable: Support/cost baseline and defect priorities.
tasks.acceptance: Do not advertise availability or service levels that are not staffed.

tasks.title: Review Day 60 conversion and channel fit
tasks.description: Check qualification and demo results, acquisition spending and time. Distinguish low volume from weak conversion.
tasks.deliverable: A/B decision with a two-week experiment if behind.
tasks.acceptance: No forecast is labeled an achieved result.

tasks.title: Complete pilot success and purchase reviews
tasks.description: Compare agreed success criteria, user feedback, safe operation and real support cost; obtain a separate voluntary purchase decision.
tasks.deliverable: Two reviewed pilot outcome records.
tasks.acceptance: No automatic paid conversion or coerced subscription.

tasks.title: Run bounded alternative channel tests
tasks.description: If Plan A is weak, test two permitted partner/intent-led routes with fixed spend caps, one message difference and comparable qualification definitions.
tasks.deliverable: Two documented tests and a channel decision.
tasks.acceptance: If Plan A works, use the time for improving its conversion; do not add pointless experiments.

tasks.title: Build ten suitable written proposals
tasks.description: Use verified needs and readiness to prepare ten proposals; track decision path, dates, objections and explicit next steps.
tasks.deliverable: Ten suitable proposal records.
tasks.acceptance: No proposals to unsuitable or unserviceable organizations just to meet a count.

tasks.title: Grow to 20 qualified opportunities and demos
tasks.description: Review each account fit and demonstrate implemented capabilities. Keep the funnel current, with losses and no-response closed honestly.
tasks.deliverable: 20 qualified organizations and 20 demonstrations, counted separately.
tasks.acceptance: Numbers are planning assumptions requiring evidence.

tasks.title: Seek four cumulative pilots and three paid tenants
tasks.description: Offer appropriate bounded pilots and obtain actual customer purchase decisions. Verify billing and usable activation.
tasks.deliverable: Four accepted cumulative pilots; three paying active tenants if fit supports them.
tasks.acceptance: One customer is counted once; no simulated billing or verbal intention.

tasks.title: Review recurring revenue and break-even gap
tasks.description: Use actual price and margin, recurring receipts, churn, support costs and full acquisition cost. Reforecast runway weekly.
tasks.deliverable: MRR, contribution, CAC and break-even scenarios.
tasks.acceptance: Three paid tenants is validation, not a claim of platform profitability.

tasks.title: Review narrow organizational contract option
tasks.description: If B fails, consider a smaller scope or real organizational service agreement through the appropriate procurement route.
tasks.deliverable: Two qualified discussions and a viable proposal if available.
tasks.acceptance: No public contract or funding is presumed; no unsafe scope expansion.

tasks.title: Hold Day 90 and Day 180 strategic reviews
tasks.description: Compare milestones, quality, actual cash and available support. Record continue, narrow, pivot or pause plus named actions.
tasks.deliverable: Evidence-backed decisions and next cycle proposal.
tasks.acceptance: Pause if critical access failures, payroll risk or no viable unit economics remain.

tasks.title: Day 90 monthly evidence and funding review
tasks.description: Review actual funnel stages, receipts, delivery cost, staffing / support, quality exceptions and cash runway. Explain every unmet target, assign a dated corrective action and choose continue, narrow, pivot or HOLD.
tasks.deliverable: Signed monthly evidence review, spend decision and owner/deadline list.
tasks.acceptance: The reviewer reconciles source records and preserves patient choice, access security and funded commitments. No progress is invented.

weeklyRhythm: Monday: confirm qualified demand, cash and staffed capacity; assign one owner to each blocker.
Wednesday: review safety, access, incidents and delivery exceptions; resolve or HOLD.
Friday: review actual funnel stages, spending, unit economics, missing evidence and the next bounded action.
Days 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180: retain a signed decision and complete a finance/quality review.
master.summary: Validate a narrow B2B platform offer, prove tenant-safe workflows, then seek four bounded pilots and three paying active organizations by Day 180. This is a validation cohort, not platform break-even.
finance: Illustration only: CAD399 recurring monthly fee × 3 active paying tenants = CAD1,197 end-period MRR; price and demand are unvalidated.

At 70% contribution and CAD5,000 monthly fixed costs plus CAD1,000/month acquisition allocation, break-even is ceiling(6000/(399×0.70)) = 22 paying tenants. Three tenants do not fund this assumed overhead.

Six-month gross funding envelope before receipts: CAD30,000 fixed + CAD6,000 acquisition + CAD4,000 setup + CAD6,000 contingency = CAD46,000. Include founder/support time and tax/payment effects in actual quotes.

CAC = all attributable sales + marketing costs / newly paying tenants. CAD6,000 / 3 = CAD2,000 only if this covers every attributable acquisition cost. Do not project lifetime value before retention evidence.
Approve actual budget by Day 21; release at most a proposed CAD1,500 first acquisition tranche after readiness. Reprice, reduce cost or narrow the model if the payback/runway is not viable.
fallbacks: A: by Day 60 seek 8 qualified organizations and 8 useful demos after readiness. If fewer than 4 suitable opportunities or recurring product-fit objections persist, diagnose before spending more.
B: two bounded two-week channel/message tests during Days 61–120; compare qualified opportunities and fully loaded CAC, not clicks.
C: by Day 150 test a narrower workflow/service or formal organizational pilot. If no viable paid use case and under eight weeks funded cash remain, pause acquisition and protect existing commitments.

tasks.title: Confirm two neighbourhoods and narrow care scope
tasks.description: Choose two initial local areas, travel window, service pathways, staffed hours, exclusions and admission limits.
tasks.deliverable: Written scope and availability sheet.
tasks.acceptance: RN and operations approve what can actually be delivered.

tasks.title: Verify RN lead and clinical backup
tasks.description: Verify registration, competence, liability, availability, backup and escalation. Recruit real cover before using RN-led claims.
tasks.deliverable: Credential references and coverage agreement.
tasks.acceptance: A proposed role is not evidence of clinical availability.

tasks.title: Complete 15 family/caregiver interviews
tasks.description: Ask about existing services, unmet tasks, communication, affordability and switching barriers with permission.
tasks.deliverable: 15 de-identified interview records and offer changes.
tasks.acceptance: No clinical histories or promotional consent assumptions in research notes.

tasks.title: Hold ten clinical and five community discussions
tasks.description: Use organization-approved routes to understand service gaps, suitable referrals and venue permissions.
tasks.deliverable: Ten clinical and five community discovery notes.
tasks.acceptance: No recruiting an employer’s patients, promised partnerships or patient direction payments.

tasks.title: Review service contracts and privacy flow
tasks.description: Separate care, information-sharing and marketing consent; review records, scope, itemized fees, cancellation and safe transfer.
tasks.deliverable: Approved policy/contract versions and open issues.
tasks.acceptance: Resolve critical privacy and consent gaps before service.

tasks.title: Approve assessment, care-plan and escalation process
tasks.description: Define consent, assessment, goals, authorized tasks, staff competence, version approval, observations, reassessment and urgent handoff.
tasks.deliverable: Clinical workflow and test case evidence.
tasks.acceptance: Professional judgment remains with qualified clinicians.

tasks.title: Verify competent roster and backup drill
tasks.description: Match planned visits with qualified primary/backup cover; simulate a missed essential visit and absence.
tasks.deliverable: Capacity sheet and recovery-drill record.
tasks.acceptance: No admissions above safe capacity; essential-care failures trigger hold.

tasks.title: Test intake, SMS verification and human recovery
tasks.description: Use test accounts for enquiries, country-code handling, OTP entry, failure, staffed callback, authorization and audit readback.
tasks.deliverable: End-to-end test/defect references and recovered failures.
tasks.acceptance: Unavailable verification must reach a real safe human route before growth.

tasks.title: Replace cost inputs and secure cash cover
tasks.description: Quote wages, RN cover, insurance, travel, recruitment and marketing. Model variable margin, weekly receipts and four-week direct-cost float.
tasks.deliverable: Quote-backed rates and downside cash plan.
tasks.acceptance: Do not commit payroll or expansion without a viable funded plan.

tasks.title: Review truthful accessible service information
tasks.description: Explain actual scope, price and public options using readable phone/print/web routes. Check nursing advertising rules before publishing.
tasks.deliverable: Reviewed factual service sheet and accessible enquiry route.
tasks.acceptance: No superiority guarantees, referral rewards or nursing-client testimonials.

tasks.title: Quote and design the awareness experiment
tasks.description: Obtain print, contextual digital and venue quotes. Define senior audience proxies, caregiver reach and overlap limits.
tasks.deliverable: Two-area channel plan with source codes and spend caps.
tasks.acceptance: 50k is gross estimated opportunity, not proven unique seniors.

tasks.title: Approve Day 30 launch gate
tasks.description: Review all six readiness domains and actual support capacity. Record HOLD or a bounded pilot release.
tasks.deliverable: Six evidence reviews and signed operating decision.
tasks.acceptance: Calendar dates never override unresolved safety, privacy or cover problems.

tasks.title: Operate a controlled first-family pilot
tasks.description: Accept only suitable consenting clients after readiness. Use written costs and the individual care plan; support existing providers and public options.
tasks.deliverable: Up to five actual active families, with review records.
tasks.acceptance: No unsuitable admissions to meet a count; no unstaffed availability claims.

tasks.title: Run early clinical and patient-choice reviews
tasks.description: Review new clients at the agreed early intervals and after changes; check understanding, costs, continuity and continuing need.
tasks.deliverable: Review-due list and documented follow-up references.
tasks.acceptance: All applicable reviews need a denominator; safe discharge and choice take priority.

tasks.title: Activate three approved community pathways
tasks.description: Seek institutional permission, confirm suitable scope and capacity, and test consented acknowledgement and acceptance/decline follow-up.
tasks.deliverable: Three approved pathway records if organizations agree.
tasks.acceptance: No referral commissions, patient lists or implied endorsements.

tasks.title: Release the first awareness tranche
tasks.description: After readiness, run small permitted channels and patient-initiated search. Publish staffed availability; measure source and qualified fit.
tasks.deliverable: Weekly spend/reach/enquiry evidence; first tranche capped at CAD2,500.
tasks.acceptance: Spend ceiling is a planning cap, not an instruction to buy ads now.

tasks.title: Qualify and assess the enquiry funnel
tasks.description: Record permission, need, service fit and cost understanding, then arrange professional assessment only when appropriate.
tasks.deliverable: 120 qualified enquiries and 60 assessments as hypotheses.
tasks.acceptance: No unnecessary clinical assessments or use of clinical records for marketing.

tasks.title: Audit every applicable pilot care plan
tasks.description: Check consent, clinical owner, current version, assigned tasks, staff scope, review date and authorized contacts for every applicable active record.
tasks.deliverable: Applicable-record denominator and review evidence.
tasks.acceptance: Zero active clients is not 100% compliance; resolve serious exceptions before new admissions.

tasks.title: Review Day 60 demand, care and cash
tasks.description: Compare five active families, qualified demand, approved pathways, missed visits, cover, contribution and cash.
tasks.deliverable: Continue / B-test / HOLD decision with corrective tasks.
tasks.acceptance: No broad marketing if quality, staffing or contribution fails.

tasks.title: Reach Day 90 awareness and active-client milestone
tasks.description: Deepen proven permitted channels, publish real capacity and prepare staff before demand. Track 25k gross opportunities and ten active families separately.
tasks.deliverable: 25k estimated opportunities, 100 enquiries and ten active families if viable.
tasks.acceptance: Reach, enquiries and active clients are different measures; no mixing them.

tasks.title: Monitor scheduled delivery and missed-care recovery
tasks.description: Review completed scheduled visits, continuity, complaints and any essential-care failures weekly. Use denominators and escalation.
tasks.deliverable: Delivery report, incident references and closed recovery actions.
tasks.acceptance: 95% nonessential-visit completion is an internal target; every essential miss needs immediate review.

tasks.title: Run Plan B tests only when justified
tasks.description: If partner traction is weak, run two bounded two-week patient/caregiver-initiated channel tests; isolate a message variable and compare qualified fit.
tasks.deliverable: Two experiments or a documented reason to keep Plan A.
tasks.acceptance: No health-list targeting, fear claims or extra spend hiding poor service.

tasks.title: Train and add staffed capacity before expansion
tasks.description: Recruit, verify and orient competent cover as needed. Recalculate travel, productive hours and RN review demand before new bookings.
tasks.deliverable: Updated roster, training and safe admission limit.
tasks.acceptance: The sample 20-family model needs 160 planned service hours/week and relevant RN cover, not just accounts in a database.

tasks.title: Build six-month awareness and enquiry results
tasks.description: Use winning channels and staged budgets toward 50k gross opportunities and 240 enquiries. Deduplicate consented enquiries and report uncertainty.
tasks.deliverable: Channel evidence, 50k opportunities and 240 voluntary enquiries if feasible.
tasks.acceptance: The 0.48% enquiry hypothesis must be revised from actual results.

tasks.title: Review admissions, continuing need and exits

tasks.deliverable: Start/active/exit counts plus patient-choice review references.
tasks.acceptance: Four exits is a planning assumption; do not retain unnecessary care.

weeklyRhythm: Monday: confirm qualified demand, cash and staffed capacity; assign one owner to each blocker.
Wednesday: review safety, access, incidents and delivery exceptions; resolve or HOLD.

tenant.summary: Start with a verified local care service. Test 50,000 gross awareness opportunities, 240 enquiries, 120 qualified enquiries, 60 suitable assessments, 24 suitable starts and 20 active families by Day 180, subject to need, consent, safe capacity and cash.
finance: Illustration only: CAD52 PSW bill rate − CAD32 loaded delivery cost − CAD4 other variable cost = CAD16 contribution/hour. Nursing services need their own validated price/scope.

At 20 active families × 8 appropriate hours/week × 4.33 weeks, end-period revenue is CAD36,026 and contribution CAD11,085. Less CAD8,000 fixed and CAD1,667/month marketing allocation leaves about CAD1,418 before tax/setup. This is a steady-state example, not cumulative profit.

Illustrative capacity: 8 PSW FTE equivalents × 25 productive hours × 80% planned use = 160 hours/week, supporting 20 clients at 8 hours. RN review/backup need separate verified cover. Do not prescribe more hours to meet revenue targets.

Six-month gross envelope before receipts remains about CAD91,040: fixed 48k + marketing 10k + setup 4k + contingency 6k + four-week direct-service float 23,040. Avoid double counting the float in cash forecasts.

Illustrative fully allocated acquisition cost: CAD10,000 marketing + CAD3,000 acquisition labour already included in fixed costs, divided by 24 starts = CAD542/start; about 4.2 weeks of CAD128/client weekly contribution before fixed costs. Replace every input with actual records.
fallbacks: A: approved professional/community pathways and local patient-initiated demand. Seek three pathways and five appropriate active families by Day 60, conditional on readiness.

B: if pathways or qualified demand are weak, run two bounded two-week caregiver/patient-initiated tests. Review at least 20 qualified enquiries before drawing an early conversion conclusion; small samples remain uncertain.

C: narrow geography/scope or seek a genuine scoped organizational contract. Pause growth if contribution is negative, essential-care failures recur, cover is absent or funded runway falls below eight weeks.
